audit.whatIsWrong: Three rows disagree with the packet chart and with their own reasons. Both layers read Skill / Rumble / Rumble / Skill / Skill / Rumble / Rumble, while whys[2] gives Neeko 'a trade he can't answer' and whys[5] describes her first-item spike. The packet chart is Skill / Skill / Neeko / Skill / Neeko / Skill / Rumble, which is also the shape a 50% win rate implies: a flat lane with two Neeko windows and one Rumble stage at the end.
audit.why: Level 3 is the one stage Neeko clearly owns before her ult — Flamespitter is a 3-second cone on a 10s cooldown at rank 1, so a baited Q leaves him with nothing while Tangle-Barbs and a re-bloom land for free. The chart gave that row to Rumble.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2 and 5 flipped as matched full+content pairs (Skill / Neeko / Skill), with the Level 3 rating raised and the 2+ items rating dropped so the numbers agree with the sides.

audit.why: Four spikes with the right timings — her Level 3 bait-and-root, her Level 6, her first item, and his late scaling — and the mirror recorded both of its spikes rewritten with real mechanics and cooldowns from Rumble's side, which agrees with this shape.

audit.whatIsWrong: (a) THE WHOLE GREEN-LIGHT SYSTEM POINTS AT THE WRONG THING. focus.text, loading, winCon, enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], dosFull[2], report[1], report[3], report[5] and report[9] all build the matchup around tracking Scrap Shield. Scrap Shield is a flat 6-second cooldown — it is back before you have finished walking up, and no plan can be scheduled around it. The resource that actually governs this lane is Heat: at 50% he enters Danger Zone and every basic ability is empowered, and at 100% he Overheats and CANNOT CAST AT ALL for the duration. Neither Danger Zone nor Overheat is mentioned anywhere on the full layer. (b) dosFull[2].d calls Scrap Shield a 'fifteen-second' cooldown; it is 6s. (c) tradeBad, dontsFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d warn about 'a mobile champion' and 'whiffing it into a dash' — Rumble has no dash, which the content layer itself relies on in whys[4] ('he has no dash to escape the channel'). (d) MISSING: Electro Harpoon reduces Magic Resist as well as slowing, and he carries two charges at 850 range — his own poke is what makes his follow-up burst land harder.
audit.why: A player told to wait for a 6-second shield will never find a window and will conclude the advice is noise. Told to watch the Heat bar instead, they get a real, repeatable window where a champion with no dash literally cannot answer Tangle-Barbs into Pop Blossom.
audit.corrected: Track Heat. Danger Zone at 50% means his cone, shield and harpoons are all empowered — do not step in. Overheat at 100% locks him out of casting entirely and is the commit window. Flamespitter is 600 range, 3 seconds of burn, 10/9/8/7/6s. Electro Harpoon is 850 range, two charges, slows and shreds MR. The Equalizer is 1750 range on 130s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most punishable moment in the matchup — Overheat — is absent, while a 6s shield is named eleven times as the thing to count.
audit.why: Overheat is a hard cast lockout on a champion with no mobility. That is the window for a 12s root into a 120s ultimate, and nothing else in his kit comes close.
audit.corrected: Repointed focus.text, loading, winCon, dosFull[0], report[5] and report[9] at the Heat bar and the Overheat window.

notes: FALSE POSITIVES CONFIRMED: packet suspectNames flagged 'His Equalizer' in spikes[3].text and 'His Flamespitter' in late. Both are Rumble's real abilities (The Equalizer, Flamespitter) and neither needed changing. The genuine defect the scanner missed is bigger: the page's entire tracked-cooldown system was aimed at Scrap Shield, a flat 6-second ability, and called it fifteen seconds. Heat — Danger Zone at 50%, Overheat and a full cast lockout at 100% — appears nowhere on the full layer and only glancingly in one content string, despite being the mechanic that decides every trade. CHART CONFIDENCE: medium rather than high on rows 1 and 5. The packet chart and the page's whys agree on row 2 and row 6 but read slightly differently on 1 and 5; I followed the packet, which also matches the 50% win rate, and left the whys text alone rather than bending it to fit. The mirror recorded no chart change from Rumble's side, so nothing here contradicts it. Mirror also noted outstanding wrong-gender references to Neeko in the Rumble block's full layer — same global he/his -> she/her sweep still pending.
